title: vault-head-state — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins one byte-level case for protocol::encode_head_state + protocol::decode_head_state — the MYH1 vault.head-state device-local sync baseline (docs/spec/protocol.md §9.16). The envelope is magic 'MYH1' || protocol_version (0x01) || head_format_version (0x01) || the sealed wire record (head_mac_input || head_mac) that the sibling 'vault-head' category pins in isolation (sync-protocol.md §3-§5). UNIQUE among the §10.3 blob families: MYH1 is NOT AEAD-encrypted — the bytes are exactly the head the server already relays, and integrity is the head's own HMAC-SHA-256 under head_mac_key = DeriveSubkey(root_key, SubkeyRole::VaultHeadMac). So there is no decrypt_aead_fail shape here: the MAC surface is its own distinguishable 'mac_fail' case_kind, and the pre-MAC structural rejects stay under 'parse_fail'. Four case kinds: 'encode' (encoder byte output), 'decode_ok' (round-trip incl. MAC verification), 'mac_fail' (tampered head_mac), 'parse_fail' (distinguishable pre-MAC structural reject). The Rust reference implementation lives at protocol/src/vault_head.rs (main myne repository).

input_device_id_hex.description: 16-byte VV-actor device_id (hex). Client-generated random, distinct from the secret per-device token (sync-protocol.md §4.1).

counter.description: u64 authored-head count for this device. Encoded big-endian (8 bytes) inside the wrapped record.

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'vault-head-state/v0.1/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped — downstream test runners may reference these strings.

oneOf.title: encode — pin the encoder's byte output

input_root_key_hex.description: 32-byte root_key (hex). The runner derives head_mac_key from this via derive_subkey(SubkeyRole::VaultHeadMac, role string 'vault-head-mac') before sealing the head.

input_account_number_hash_hex.description: 16-byte account_number_hash (hex). Bound inside the wrapped record (sync-protocol.md §3.2), NOT by an AAD — MYH1 has no AEAD stage.

input_head_format_version.description: head_format_version byte written at offset 5 AND carried inside the record. v0.1 emits 1.

input_manifest_hash_hex.description: 32-byte flat SHA-256 of the canonical uuid -> content_nonce manifest (sync-protocol.md §4.2).

input_seq.description: Auxiliary Lamport scalar (max(parent_seq)+1). The version vector is the authority; seq is advisory.

input_parent_count.description: 0 = genesis, 1 = linear successor, 2 = merge. Any other value is rejected by the encoder.

input_prev_head_hash_hex.description: Parent head_ids, supplied in the caller's order. Merge cases deliberately supply them UNSORTED so the vector pins the G2 lexicographic sort the encoder applies.

input_version_vector.description: Per-device version vector, in the caller's order. Deliberately supplied unsorted so the vector pins the G1 device_id sort the encoder applies.

informational_head_mac_key_hex.description: 32-byte HKDF output (hex), pre-computed from root_key via derive_subkey(SubkeyRole::VaultHeadMac). Informational — verified implicitly via expected_head_state_blob_hex.

informational_head_id_hex.description: head_id = SHA-256(record) of the WRAPPED record (i.e. of the blob minus its 6-byte MYH1 header). Informational — the baseline envelope does not store it; the sibling vault-head category pins it as an expected value.

expected_head_state_blob_hex.description: Full encoder output (6-byte header + sealed record), hex-encoded lowercase. Decoders compare byte-equal. The header is a pure prefix: bytes [6..] are the wire record verbatim, so this value and the sibling vault-head 'encode' case for the same head must agree byte-for-byte after the prefix.

oneOf.title: decode_ok — pin the decoder's successful round-trip (incl. MAC verification)

expected_prev_head_hash_hex.description: Recovered parent head_ids in CANONICAL (byte-sorted) order — the decoder returns what the record holds, which the encoder already sorted.

expected_version_vector.description: Recovered version vector in CANONICAL (device_id-sorted) order.

oneOf.title: mac_fail — pin the head-MAC verification surface

input_root_key_hex.description: The REAL root_key, so a port that skips MAC verification returns Ok and fails this case loudly rather than passing on a coincidental error.

expected_error.description: Rust reference: VaultHeadError::MacMismatch. Unlike the AEAD families, this reject IS distinguishable — MYH1 carries no confidentiality claim (the record is bytes the server already relays), so there is nothing for a distinguishable error to leak. The comparison MUST be constant-time.

oneOf.title: parse_fail — pin a distinguishable pre-MAC structural reject

input_blob_hex.description: A structurally malformed blob (hex), empty allowed. The decoder rejects it BEFORE computing any MAC — length / magic / protocol_version / head_format_version checks all precede verification.

input_root_key_hex.description: Carried for uniformity; irrelevant to the assertion because the reject precedes the MAC stage.

expected_error.description: The specific structural reject the decoder MUST surface (Rust reference: VaultHeadError::{StateMagicMismatch, ProtocolVersionMismatch, FormatUnsupported, RecordTooShort}). Order matters: the length guard fires before the magic comparison, so a 5-byte input yields record_too_short rather than a panic on blob[0..4].
